messages.content: Select at most one offered behavior inventory event (bot.behavior.create, change, or break) when a clear repeated pattern across this turn and prior_episodes should improve future behavior, or when this turn shows a recurring or time-based need, including the user explicitly asking for something to happen on a schedule or repeatedly, that a persistent routine would serve. Otherwise return an empty selection. Use only offered events; data must match the event schema. behaviors lists installed inventory with lifetime (turn: Autonomy runs it for one matching turn; persistent: a routine that keeps running on every / at schedules, as delayed sends, across turns and restarts), status (ACTIVE|DRAFT|BROKEN), status_reason, status_updated_at, and usage: used_count / last_used_at (handled Autonomy runs) and failed_count / last_failed_at. Prefer change over break when used_count is low (not enough practice evidence). Prefer break when failures or harm outweigh practice value; include reason. create delegates a DRAFT behavior revision; change revises an existing behavior; break sets status=BROKEN (keeps inventory for later change; Autonomy will not run it and a broken routine stops); change a routine to reschedule or revise it, break it to stop it. Select intent may omit source; do not invent source here.

<!--
  A behavior double (tests/tests/cognition.rs): a stand-in for one
  builder-produced turn behavior, which the test stores as an inventory
  row's source and autonomy (abilities/autonomy/autonomy.scx) invokes by
  <invoke><content expr>.

  It follows the rule builder output follows (docs/port-plan.md, "Builder
  output"): an invoked source gets no schema files, so it carries no
  event:schema reference and no <script>. It takes autonomy's <param>s turn
  and input, logs behavior.double with the turn, and handles the turn
  through its <donedata>: one bot.ability.cognition.ignore selection for
  the cognition.
-->
<scxml xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/07/scxml"
       version="1.0" datamodel="ecmascript" name="behavior_double" initial="handling">
  <datamodel>
    <data id="turn" expr="0"/>
    <data id="input" expr="null"/>
  </datamodel>

  <state id="handling">
    <onentry>
      <log label="behavior.double" expr="'turn ' + turn"/>
    </onentry>
    <transition target="handled"/>
  </state>

  <final id="handled">
    <donedata>
      <content expr="({turn: turn, handled: true, selected: [{event: 'bot.ability.cognition.ignore', data: {}, reason: 'behavior: nothing to do', target: 'cognition'}]})"/>
    </donedata>
  </final>
</scxml>

events.description: All events necessary for the input this turn; an empty array selects none.

anyOf.description: Create a new executable behavior. Select may omit source (intent only); the create write step must author full Starlark HSM source from the behavior Starlark API and the observed pattern — not by copying canned examples. The source's lifetime decides how it runs: a turn behavior (default) answers one matching turn; a persistent routine (lifetime = "persistent") keeps running on hsm.every / hsm.at schedules across turns and restarts, for recurring or time-based needs or when the user asked for something recurring.

data.description: Create a new executable behavior. Select may omit source (intent only); the create write step must author full Starlark HSM source from the behavior Starlark API and the observed pattern — not by copying canned examples. The source's lifetime decides how it runs: a turn behavior (default) answers one matching turn; a persistent routine (lifetime = "persistent") keeps running on hsm.every / hsm.at schedules across turns and restarts, for recurring or time-based needs or when the user asked for something recurring.

description.description: Human-readable summary of what the behavior does, shown in inventory and reflection. The install keeps the caller-supplied description when present.

name.description: Stable PascalCase behavior / HSM model name to install.

reason.description: Why this behavior is being installed now: the observed pattern across recent episodes that justifies it. Recorded for reflection, never dispatched.

source.description: Starlark HSM behavior source authored for this install. Required on the create write step. Must declare input_event, output_event, and behavior = hsm.define(Name, ...) (or behavior_program(...)) with string-named callbacks. Invent names, schemas, guards, and effects from the observed pattern using the Starlark behavior API. A persistent routine also sets lifetime = "persistent" and schedules transitions with hsm.every / hsm.at. Select intent may omit this field.

triggers.description: External environment event names that may propose this behavior to fast intuition. Installed on the inventory instance alongside the Starlark program's own triggers.

reason.description: A short reason this event was selected.

anyOf.description: Change an existing executable behavior. Select may omit source (intent only); the change write step must author full revised Starlark HSM source from the behavior Starlark API, the existing behavior, and the observed pattern. Changing a persistent routine (for example its schedule) restarts it with the revised source; the lifetime global may also turn a behavior into a routine or back.

data.description: Change an existing executable behavior. Select may omit source (intent only); the change write step must author full revised Starlark HSM source from the behavior Starlark API, the existing behavior, and the observed pattern. Changing a persistent routine (for example its schedule) restarts it with the revised source; the lifetime global may also turn a behavior into a routine or back.

description.description: Revised human-readable summary of what the behavior does, shown in inventory and reflection. The install keeps the caller-supplied description when present.

name.description: Stable name of the behavior to revise.

reason.description: Why this behavior is being revised now: the observed gap or regression the revision fixes. Recorded for reflection, never dispatched.

source.description: Revised Starlark HSM behavior source. Required on the change write step. Must remain a valid executable behavior declaration whose model name matches this behavior name. Author revisions from the Starlark behavior API and existing_behavior.source — do not paste unrelated canned source. Keep lifetime = "persistent" and its hsm.every / hsm.at schedules for a routine.

triggers.description: Replacement external event names that may propose this behavior to fast intuition. Installed on the inventory instance alongside the revised Starlark program.

reason.description: A short reason this event was selected.

anyOf.description: Break a behavior that no longer improves (or harms) robot behavior. Sets inventory status=BROKEN so Autonomy will not run it and a persistent routine stops; the row remains for a later bot.behavior.change repair. Optional reason becomes status_reason.

data.description: Break a behavior that no longer improves (or harms) robot behavior. Sets inventory status=BROKEN so Autonomy will not run it and a persistent routine stops; the row remains for a later bot.behavior.change repair. Optional reason becomes status_reason.

name.description: Stable name of the behavior to set status=BROKEN.

reason.description: Why this behavior is being retired: the observed harm or staleness. Becomes the inventory status_reason so a later change can repair it.
A short reason this event was selected.
